name: Allicin
summary: Allicin is a organosulfur compound associated with garlic.
description: Allicin is an organosulfur compound formed from garlic; preclinical data suggest antimicrobial and redox effects, but it is chemically unstable in humans.
safetyNotes: Unstable compound; safety inferred from garlic intake
evidenceLevel: Editorial grade not demonstrated by recorded studies
contraindications: Bleeding disorders or anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy without clinician review
scheduled surgery (discontinue high-dose garlic-derived supplements 1-2 weeks prior)
pregnancy/breastfeeding at concentrated supplemental doses without guidance
May increase bleeding risk with anticoagulants/antiplatelets such as warfarin or aspirin or clopidogrel
may potentiate antidiabetic and antihypertensive medications
garlic constituents have been reported to reduce plasma levels of saquinavir and other CYP3A4-metabolized drugs.
